Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ctsem 4.0.0

14/10/2026

A major release. ctsem has a second estimation engine, written in Julia, which most of the new features below need and which is now the default for ctFit(). Use backend='stan' for the previous behaviour.

  • New backend='julia' for ctFit(), with exact gradients and Hessians, using multiple cores. ctJuliaInstall() installs Julia and the engine, asking before each download, and ctJuliaStatus(), ctJuliaSetup(), ctJuliaProcesses() and ctJuliaKill() manage Julia sessions.
  • Random effects on any parameter, including variances, nonlinear dynamics and non-Gaussian indicators, are integrated with a Laplace approximation (intoverpop='laplace', the default when optimising). Each fit checks the approximation, and intoverpop='quadrature' refines the fit where needed. Julia backend only.
  • Nested grouping levels, such as id=c('person','couple'). Each parameter’s indvarying names the levels it varies at, and poprank can be set per level. Julia backend only.
  • Ordinal, count and censored indicators, and lower and upper asymptotes for binary indicators (ASYMPTOTES in ctModel()). Julia backend only.
  • Posterior sampling with ctFit(backend='julia', optimize=FALSE), or with ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') after an optimised fit. Sampling continues until the target effective sample size is reached.
  • Smooth effects of time independent predictors, such as ctModel(TIpredNames = ~ s(age) + sex), with the smoothness estimated from the data. ctTIpredEffects(fit, whichTIpreds = 'age') shows the estimated effect. Julia backend only.
  • Sampling weights, one per subject, with ctFit(weights=). Fits maximise the weighted pseudo-likelihood and report robust standard errors. See the sampling weights vignette. Julia backend only.
  • ctOptimUncertainty() is renamed ctFitUncertainty(), and the old name still works. New methods include 'sample', 'stored' to draw again from the covariance stored with a fit, and importance sampling against the quadrature or particle filter likelihood (intoverpop='quadrature', filter='particle').
  • New uncertainty='checked', which checks the Hessian’s normal approximation and uses importance sampling where it does not hold. uncertainty='surrogate' is removed. Use 'checked' instead.
  • On the julia backend, missing values of time independent predictors are imputed when optimising and sampled when sampling, and nlcontrol$nsubsteps='auto' chooses the number of integration steps for a nonlinear model.
  • ctFit(stationary=TRUE) works again, with backend='julia'.
  • Model matrix cells accept a named form, 'mm, indvarying=TRUE, sdscale=0.5', as well as 'mm||TRUE|0.5'. ctPar() writes either form, and ctCov() writes a covariance matrix as cells.
  • Covariance matrices are parameterised by a matrix logarithm, so any positive definite matrix can be reached. Use model$covmattransform='rawcorr' for the previous parameterisation.
  • A parameter used in cells with different default transforms, such as a DRIFT diagonal and an off-diagonal, now gives an error. Previously each cell transformed it differently.
  • New checks: ctReport() runs the reporting and checking functions on a fit and saves the results to a folder. ctIdentify() and ctFitProfile() check identification on the julia backend, ctLaplaceCheck() and ctParticleLik() check the approximations a julia fit makes, and ctTracePlot() plots a julia fit’s optimisation or chains.
  • New plots of the dynamics: ctNetwork(), ctNetworkPlot(), ctPhasePortrait(), ctStateDependencePlot() and ctVarianceDecomposition().
  • Posterior predictive checks are combined in ctPostPredPlots(), with panels for the mean trajectory and the lagged covariance. ctFitCovCheck() is renamed ctFitCheckCov() and can split by group. The old name still works.
  • ctLOO(method='psis') cross-validates a Laplace fit without refitting.
  • coef(), vcov(), logLik(), print() and anova(), a likelihood ratio test table for nested fits, work for fits from either backend, and summary(), plot() and ctPlotPosterior() for julia fits.
  • For fits made with priors=TRUE, ctChisqTest() now compares log likelihoods. It compared log posteriors before.
  • ctGenerate(fromPriors=TRUE) generates data sets from a model’s prior predictive distribution, without a fit or data, and ctGenerateFromPriors() is deprecated. ctGenerate(backend='julia') generates random effects at every level, nonlinear dynamics and non-Gaussian indicators. It fills in a given design with datastruct=, and takes population values with values=, on the scales summary() reports.
  • ctGenerate()’s n.subjects is now n, one count per id level. n.subjects still works, with a warning.
  • ACF plots fit a precision weighted spline by default, method='weighted'. Use method='quantile' for the previous plot.
  • Functions that run fits or engine loops use cores=getOption('mc.cores', 2) by default, as ctFit() does. For ctOptimUncertainty(), ctFitCovCheck() and ctKalmanArray() this is up from one. Use cores=1 for the previous behaviour.
  • When sampling, ctFit() uses getOption('mc.cores', 2) cores by default. It used one per chain before. Use cores='maxneeded' for the previous behaviour.
  • uncertainty='is' samples adaptively, and warns when the Pareto k of its weights exceeds 0.7. Its effective sample size target is now 200. Use optimcontrol$isESS=100 for the previous target.
  • ctDiscretePars(), ctPredictTIP(), ctExtract() and ctKalmanArray() select subjects by their ids in the data, as ctPredict() does. Use realid=FALSE for the previous behaviour.
  • ctDiscretePars()’s observational is deprecated in favour of impulseType. 'unit' replaces observational=FALSE and 'observed' replaces observational=TRUE.
  • For a model whose dynamics depend on the state, ctDiscretePars() on a julia fit now uses the drift’s Jacobian at the evaluation point, which is the model linearised there. ctSummaryMatrices(fit, state=)$DRIFT gives DRIFT’s value at that point.
  • ctFit()’s iter, chains and control are deprecated in favour of entries of sampleControl. They still work, with a warning.
  • ctModelCoverage_check() is renamed ctCoverageCheck(), with camelCase arguments. The old name is defunct.
  • ctCheckFit() is defunct, replaced by ctPostPredPlots() and ctFitCheckCov().
  • ctFitUpdateModel() and ctStanUpdModel() are defunct. Use ctFitUpdate().
  • The vb argument of ctFit() (Stan’s variational inference) is removed.
  • Fixed: standard errors for combinations of parameters the data do not identify came from numerical rounding, and could inflate the standard errors of other parameters. Such parameters are now reported as unidentified.
  • Fixed: computing quantities over several posterior draws with cores > 1 could stop with a Stan exception, or return draws out of order, in ctGenerateFromPriors(), ctKalman(), ctPredict() and plot().
  • Fixed: backend='stan' with optimcontrol$estonly=TRUE failed for models with time independent predictors, which also stopped ctLOO().
  • Fixed: a time independent predictor effect fixed to a value, such as age=0.5, was ignored by backend='stan'. Stan now gives an error for such effects, and backend='julia' fits them.
  • Fixed: with backend='stan', a continuous time model whose DIFFUSION differed between subjects while DRIFT did not used the previous subject’s diffusion for a subject whose first time interval equalled the previous subject’s last.
  • Fixed: ctACF() and ctACFresiduals() dropped lag 0 from cross correlations.
  • Fixed: ctACF() and ctACFresiduals() counted pairs of observations at the wrong time lags unless every time fell on the time step’s grid, which could show large spurious correlations. ctDiscretiseData() left such times off its grid, and shifted every time by an offset.
  • Fixed: ctDiscretePars() given subjects out of ascending order labelled each subject’s results with another’s id.
  • Fixed: ctIntervalise() read columns by position, so wide data with ctsem’s column names in another order had values moved to the wrong variable and occasion. Columns are now matched by name. It also set observations at other occasions to missing where an occasion’s time was missing.
  • Fixed: ctPredictTIP()’s dynamics panels gave curves each other’s labels when two or more moderator values were negative, as for a centred moderator, and with several predictors could show another predictor’s curves.
  • Fixed: data values that do not read as numbers were treated as missing. ctFit() now stops and names them.
  • Fixed: in a nonlinear model, a cell using min() or max() of a state was linearised as if it did not depend on that state.
  • Fixed: ctGenerate() stopped with an error for a model with a DRIFT diagonal of 0, such as a linear trend.

ctsem 3.11.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-30

29/6/2026

  • Function names have been simplified to remove Stan-specific wording from the main user-facing API. Use ctFit() rather than ctStanFit(), and the new non-Stan helper names such as ctGenerateFromPriors(), ctGenerateFromFit(), ctPlotPosterior(), ctPostPredict(), ctSubjectPars(), ctTIpredEffects(), and ctSummaryMatrices(). The old names remain as compatibility aliases for existing code. See the ctsem GitHub repository for further details: https://github.com/cdriveraus/ctsem.
  • ctFit() now uses model as the model argument name. The old ctstanmodel argument is deprecated but still accepted for existing scripts.
  • Modern fitting workflows should generally use ctModel(type='ct') or ctModel(type='dt') followed by ctFit(). ctModel(type='omx') objects are retained primarily for data generation and legacy workflows; convert them with ctModelConvertOMX() before fitting in the modern ctsem format.
  • System matrices can be directly edited in the model object $matrices subobject, this will automatically update the data.frame containing full specification under $pars and vice-versa.
  • ctEmpiricalBayesFit is a new function that fits single subjects under the specified model, computes an empirical prior from those fits, then re-fits the subjects with that prior.
  • Optimized-fit uncertainty can be refreshed with ctOptimUncertainty(), including Hessian, local surrogate, one-step bootstrap, full refit bootstrap, sandwich, and outer product of gradient approximations.

ctsem 3.10.4

CRAN release: 2025-06-30

27/6/2025

  • Fixed bug in initial optimizer stages for nonlinear models requiring compilation.

ctsem 3.10.3

CRAN release: 2025-06-21

18/6/2025 - Major improvements to importance sampling. - Include ctFitCovCheck function for checking empirical vs model implied covariance over time. - Reduce parallel compute init overhead - Minor bug fixes to ctKalman - refactor stanoptimis, changes to carefulfit logic, remove DEoptim option.

ctsem 3.10.2

CRAN release: 2025-01-13

9/1/2025 - Stochastic optimizer improvements - Bootstrap uncertainty improvements – when fitting, use argument optimcontrol=list(uncertainty=‘bootstrap’)

ctsem 3.10.1

CRAN release: 2024-08-19

12/8/2024 - Fix bug introduced in 3.10.0 where certain combinations of Gaussian and binary variables cause convergence difficulties and invalid results. - Revert unconstrained correlation change introduced in 3.10.0, it was more difficult to fit in some cases. - Detect duplicated T0MEANS parameters and propose alternative approach. - Add ctPredictTIP function for examining and plotting differences due to time independent predictors.

ctsem 3.10.0

CRAN release: 2024-05-09

10/05/2024 - Fix bug when computing Jacobian of certain nonlinear models. - Modify unconstrained correlation approach for better optimization / uncertainty quantification and clearer interpretation. - Add ctACF function for plotting approximate continuous time auto and cross correlations. - Bug fixes to ctKalman plots, were occasionally confused re subject ID. - Include experimental / imperfect approach to ordinal data.

ctsem 3.9.1

CRAN release: 2023-10-30

30/10/2023 - Fix bug in ctKalman - was dropping certain subjects resulting in no plots / output. - Fix fatal (i.e, erroring out) bug in certain nonlinear parameter specifications. - Allow direct references to time dependent predictors in nonlinear specifications - now measurement model can easily depend on time varying covariates. - Update array syntax internally to rstan 2.26+ approach – completely this time…

ctsem 3.9.0

CRAN release: 2023-09-14

14/9/2023 - Add progress reports for stochastic optimizer and Hessian. - Add small noise to improve sampling performance when inits='optimize'. - Include ctACF and ctACFresiduafunction for approximate continuous time auto-correlations. - Update array syntax internally to rstan 2.26+ approach. - Improved stochastic optimizer.

ctsem 3.8.1

CRAN release: 2023-09-05

20/8/2023 - Correct bug in nonlinear formulations when the same state is referenced for multiple nonlinearities. - Correct unnecessary memory usage when computing Hessian with multiple cores. - Improve stochastic subsampling first pass optimizer. - Simplify discrete time model computations internally. - Performance gains and reduced memory usage via usage of matrix exponential subsets and automatic computation of dynamic error indices.

ctsem 3.7.6

CRAN release: 2023-03-26

20/6/2023 - Deprecate nopriors argument to ctStanFit, allow priors argument - Allow inits='optimize' argument to ctStanFit, to speed up sampling approach - Allow integer values for removeObs argument to ctKalman, for N step ahead predictions - Allow sameInitialTimes argument to ctStanFit, to generate empty observations at earliest observation time, ensuring comparability of times at T0MEANS

ctsem 3.7.6

CRAN release: 2023-03-26

24/3/2023 - Fix compile error for some higher dimensional non-linear models - Fix NaN gradient error for certain non-linear measurement error models - Use Rstantools for compile specification to ensure future compatibility - Allow standardized error output from ctKalman

ctsem 3.7.0

1/7/2022 - Fix some plotting features, speed up random effects a little

ctsem 3.6.0

CRAN release: 2022-03-10

9/3/2022 - Fix: Random effects standard deviations were mis-estimated for time-dependent predictor effects and diffusion parameters when fitting with optimization

ctsem 3.5.5

CRAN release: 2022-02-16

6/12/2021 - Some edge case optimizer problems resolved - Bug fix in discrete time plots when observational=TRUE. Correlations were unnecessarily squared previously

ctsem 3.5.4

CRAN release: 2021-07-23

22/7/2021 - Improved automatic imputation of time-independent predictors, fixed bug where too many imputed values were set to zero. Care still recommended if relying on automatic imputation though!

ctsem 3.5.3

CRAN release: 2021-06-17

16/6/2021 - Fixed bug in output of $rawpopcorr introduced in 3.4.3. Correlations displayed incorrectly, other parameters unaffected - Modified correlation approach to ensure monotonicity in high dims

ctsem 3.5.0

CRAN release: 2021-06-01

31/5/2021 - Added ctFitMultiModel function to simplify processing of multiple models - Added ctChisqTest function for simplified likelihood ratio tests between models - Added subsampling optimization for first pass, faster for larger models/data

ctsem 3.4.3

CRAN release: 2021-04-27

21/4/2021 - Changed optimization scheme, first BFGS, then stochastic gradient descent - Fixed ctStanTIpredEffects function, much faster - Altered correlation matrix approach - better optimization/sampling behavior, priors can differ by index though

ctsem 3.4.2

CRAN release: 2021-02-24

10/2/2021 - ctStanDiscretePars temporal dependence plots work for discrete time also - Fix: In certain circumstances with covariate effects on duplicated parameters, the effects may not have been completely applied in the last few releases - Other small bug fixes and efficiency improvements

ctsem 3.4

4/12/2020 - ctLOO function for leave one out/k-fold cross-validation - ctCheckFit function dramatically improved for visual model diagnostics - Fixes to a range of edge cases when specifying more complex nonlinearities - ctStanDiscretePars has improved plotting options - ctStanFitUpdate function can be used to attempt to update a saved ctStanFit object to the current version of ctsem - ctSaturatedCov function for estimating a form of saturated model as a reference. Still a bit developmental. - General robustness / efficiency improvements.

ctsem 3.3.8

CRAN release: 2020-07-16

10/7/2020 - Stationarity,subject specific parameter output, and linear system estimation removed (uses nonlinear in all cases, a bit slower) to try satisfy CRAN compile time checks.

ctsem 3.3.2

20/6/2020 - ctLOO function to compute leave k out entropy estimates for model comparison / validation. - Optimizer parallelisation for single subject models - ctStanFitUpdate function to use saved fit objects created in earlier versions of ctsem. - Multiple core memory usage reductions.

ctsem 3.2.1

CRAN release: 2020-04-26

26/4/2020 - Minor updates to suit rstan 2.2.3 - Higher dim Hessian really really fixed…

ctsem 3.2.0

CRAN release: 2020-04-21

18/4/2020 - Change to defaults of ctStanFit – optimization without priors is new default. - Optimization with binary variables much improved – specify using: mymodel$manifesttype <- c(1,0,1) for 3 manifest variables, 1st and last binary and second continuous. - Improved latex output for models and fits using ctModelLatex. - Hessian estimation in higher dimensions fixed, again. - Experimental automatic covariate (tipred) detection – set mymodel$TIpredAuto <- 1L to try it. - Minor plotting / other fixes

ctsem 3.1.1

CRAN release: 2020-02-10

10/2/2020 - Reverted to non sequential measurement update introduced in 3.1.0 - Further hessian estimation fixes - Stochastic optimizer further improved

ctsem 3.1.0

CRAN release: 2020-01-27

21/01/2020 - Fixed Hessian estimation sensitivity introduced last release. - ctStanKalman has option to return subject specific estimates. - Various performance improvements – stochastic optimizer very effective with many parameters. - Fix rounding, off by one issue when using timestep argument for nonlinear dynamics.

ctsem 3.0.9

CRAN release: 2019-12-18

10/12/2019 - ctStanGenerate function – generate from a ctstanmodel and prior distribution. - Parallel optimization improvements – memory usage halved, more cores nearly always useful. - Missing time independent predictors single imputed when optimizing. - ctModelHigherOrder function to easily add higher order structure to specified model. E.g. slow changing trends / oscillations. - various minor output / efficiency / estimation robustness improvements.

ctsem 3.0.8

CRAN release: 2019-11-07

30/10/2019 - ctStanFit bug fix: MANIFESTVAR wrongly reported as the sqrt - ctFit bug fix: Std errors of covariances were too wide when transformedParams=TRUE - TI predictor effects can be specified as the 5th element of parameter string in ctModel – “drift11 | -exp(param) | FALSE | 1 | age, gender” - Nonlinear models: Parameter names in the additional PARS matrix, and latent variables, can be referenced directly in parameters – “-exp(cognition * drift11)” instead of “-exp(state[2] * PARS[1,1]”. PARS matrix must still be specified. - Switched plotting to ggplot2, many changes / improvements.

ctsem 3.0.4

CRAN release: 2019-09-12

11/9/2019 - Removed some spurious warnings generated by last release. - Improved ctKalman function for ctStanFit results (timestep now works). - Parallelise optimization over subjects with ctStanFit (cores=xx). - Bug fix: time varying diffusion generated errors. - Use stochastic optimizer to check for improvements by default - Simplify ctModel specification – vectors interpreted as rowwise matrices, automatic dimension detection.

ctsem 3.0.1

CRAN release: 2019-08-23

20/8/2019 - fixed a few minor / error generating bugs introduced in previous release related to random effects optimization.

ctsem 3.0.0

CRAN release: 2019-07-31

28/7/2019 - parameter transformations can be specified naturally without recompilation - analytic Jacobian’s used for extended Kalman filter where possible - improved optimizer performance - generally improved performance, particularly for nonlinear systems.

ctsem 2.9.5

14/5/2019 - corrected optimization of random effects using ctStanFit - ctModelLatex function to display within subject model equation - custom calculations allowed in ctModel for linear and nonlinear approaches - Nonlinearity possible for discrete time now also - Use stochastic optimizer by default for ctStanFit – more robust

ctsem 2.9.0

CRAN release: 2019-04-13

12/4/2019 - Improved optimizer using stochastic gradient descent. - fixed bug introduced re finding start values when binary variables are used. - custom calculations can be specified and estimated using both linear and nonlinear dynamics approach. - ctStanFit is no longer available for win32 systems. - ctStanKalman function extracts system state over time.

ctsem 2.7.3

6/11/2018 - Updated for rstan 2.18.1 compatibility - Non-linear dynamics now handled using mixture of extended and unscented filters for improved speed. - Priors for hierarchical variance modified so prior for total variance has consistent shape regardless of dimension. - Optimization / importance sampling works well for many cases, see arguments using ?ctStanFit. - ctStanPostPredict produces a range of posterior predictive plots. - Various small non-critical bug fixes / updates. (see github for details)

ctsem 2.6.5

CRAN release: 2018-06-25

25/6/2018 - Fixed bug in ctStanFit introduced in previous release leading to errors in handling of missing data. - ctStanTIpredMarginal function for plotting marginal relationships between predictors and parameters.

ctsem 2.6.0

1/6/2018 - Removed need for compilation of standard models. - Unscented Kalman filter for ctStanFit: - Non-linear / time-varying / state dependent specifications now possible. - Optimization followed by importance sampling can be used instead of sampling via Stan. - Most plotting functions still not working correctly for such models. - ctCheckFit function for plotting covariance of data generated from posterior against original. - Time independent predictors can now be used independent of random effects. - Fix bug in summary preventing display when binary variables were used in fit. - Allow data sets to contain both binary and continuous variables. - More robust data import, character string id’s and jumbled order of rows now manageable. - stanWplot no longer requires shiny to be explicitly loaded. - Fix bug in ctKalman plotting function preventing interpolation. - Fix bug in additional summary matrices introduced in 2.5.0 – some were transposed. - Summary no longer returns errors when partial stationarity is set.

ctsem 2.5.0

CRAN release: 2017-10-18

27/9/2017 Fixes: - stanWplot function for trace plots while sampling with stan was not working on non windows platforms. - ctStan summary reports population standard deviations more accurately – improved delta approach. - various minor plotting improvements

Additions / Changes: - ctStanFit now handles correlation matrices differently – little substantive impact. - ctKalman can now be used to plot individual trajectories from ctFit objects and ctStanFit objects (ctStanKalman function no longer exists). - ctStanFit now handles missing data on covariate effects – time dependent predictors are set to zero, time independent predictors are imputed with a normal(0,10) prior (can adjust via the $tipredsimputedprior subobject of the ctStanModel). - ctStanFit default population standard deviation prior now changed to a regularised independence Jeffreys – previous truncated normal approach still possible because… - ctStanFit now accepts custom specifications for the population standard deviation – see the $rawhypersd , $rawhypersdlowerbound, and $hypersdtransform subobjects of the ctStanModel object. - ctStan: Plotting covariate effects via ctStanTIpredeffects function now easier to use and more versatile – can plot effects on discrete time matrices, for instance. - ctFit and ctMultigroupFit data argument changed to ‘dat’ instead of ‘datawide’, and now dataform=“long” argument can be used to use long format data (as per ctStan) directly. - additional parameter matrices shown for summary of ctStanFit objects. - ctStanParMatrices function to compute continuous time matrices for a given model and vector of free population means.

ctsem 2.4.0

CRAN release: 2017-05-17

16/5/2017 Fixes: - Time dependent predictors generated errors with the frequentist Kalman filter form since 2.2.0 - With stationary set to NULL (not the default but offered in help file) for ctFit, t0 matrices were mistakenly set to stationary. - Duplicated parameter names now allowed in a ctStanFit model.

Features: - ctGenerateFromFit generates data based on a model fitted with ctFit. - ctPostPredict generates distributions from data based on a model fitted with ctFit and plots this against the original data.

ctsem 2.3.1

CRAN release: 2017-04-06

6/4/2017 Fixes: - summary: Standard errors were not reported in some cases - ctStanFit: 2.3.0 hierarchical correlation changes were applied too broadly - ctFit: discreteTime switch no longer gives errors when traits included - ctFit: transformedParams=FALSE argument no longer throwing errors. - ctStanKalman: correct handling of missing data for plotting.

ctsem 2.3.0

CRAN release: 2017-03-07

3/3/2017 Fixes: - TRAITVAR in frequentist ctsem was incorrectly accounting for differing time intervals since v2.0.0. TRAITVAR is now (again) reported as total between subjects variance. - Default quantiles on ctStanDiscretePars adjusted to 95%. - Hierarchical correlation probabilities adjusted in ctStanFit for more consistent behaviour with high dimensional processes.

Changes: - Default to unstandardised cross effects plots.

ctsem 2.2.0

CRAN release: 2017-01-23

1/2/2017 Changes: - Time dependent predictors now have instantaneous effect in both frequentist and Bayesian approaches, and the documentation is updated to reflect this. Previously, no TDpreds affecting first time point in frequentist. Accordingly, wide data structure is changed, with an extra column per predictor and predictors now sorted by time point as for indicators. See vignette for example. - Default to 0 covariance between time dependent predictors and initial (T0) latents / traits / time independent predictors. Specify matrix as ‘free’ in ctModel to estimate instead. - Default carefulFit = TRUE for multiple groups frequentist models (ctMultigroupFit) - Improve optimization approach for ctStanFit - but still not reliable for random effects.

Fixes: - Multiple time dependent predictors with multiple processes resulted in inaccurate estimates for TDPREDEFFECT in frequentist approach of previous versions. - Prevent ctGenerate from auto-filling matrices to 0 variance. - Correct oscillating example for change in tolerance in OpenMx.

ctsem 2.1.1

CRAN release: 2017-01-07

6/1/2017 Improvements: - improved fitting of frequentist models with ctFit and ctRefineTo, due to changes to carefulFit penalisation and refining approach.

Changes: - Removed package ‘PSM’ from suggests field and vignette as requested by CRAN

Fixes: - rstan 2.14 caused problems with data import for ctStanFit - eliminated spurious warnings for ctStanFit

ctsem 2.1.0

CRAN release: 2016-12-22

20/12/2016 Features: - Empirical Bayes, experimental but can now optimize with hierarchical model (when using the Kalman filter, as per defaults) - Easy extraction and plotting of time independent predictor (covariate) effects, see ctStanTIpredEffects for example. - Added stationary argument to ctStanFit - much more efficient than setting priors on stationarity.

Bugs fixed: - incorrect number of cores spawned for parallel sessions. - optimize and variational bayes switches for ctStanFit did not work. - ctKalman would break if only 1 row of data passed in.

ctsem 2.0.0

CRAN release: 2016-11-19

18/11/2016 Features: - Hierarchical Bayesian modeling using Stan, see ctStanFit function and the vignette at https://cran.r-project.org/package=ctsem/vignettes/hierarchical.pdf

Changes: - Defaults change: Fix CINT to 0 and free MANIFESTMEANS - Reintroduce variable effect of TRAITVAR at T0 (more flexible but more fitting problems - try MANIFESTTRAITVAR instead if problematic, or use step-wise fitting approach, automated with ctRefineTo)

ctsem 1.1.6

CRAN release: 2016-06-15

Features added: - now with a change log! - ctCompareExpectation plots expected means and covariances against model implied. - remove log transform of drift matrix diagonal, positive drift diagonals again possible. - ctRefineTo allows easy step wise fitting from simple to complex - faster and more robust fitting in many cases. - ctPlot is a new function that allows more customization of plots. - ctModel now allows time varying means to be specified.

Bugs fixed: - corrected handling of Cholesky inputs for ctGenerate
